apod.explanation: Saturn vanishes when the Moon passes in front of it — an occultation visible in early 2025 from Greenland through central Europe to northern Africa. This fusion of three images from Sardinia, Italy, catches Saturn just before it disappeared; the bright dot nearby is the star 85 Aquarii, and the next such occultation comes in 2031.
apod.title: Saturn Behind the Moon

breaking.headline: $42B 10-year auction tails; foreign demand plunges
breaking.fact: The Treasury sold $42B of 10-year notes at a 5.020% high yield, tailing the when-issued level by 1bp — the biggest tail since February. Bid-to-cover fell to 2.46×, the lowest since May; indirect (foreign) bidders took just 61.2%, the lowest since October 2023, while direct bidders jumped to 29.0%, the highest since September 2013.

breaking.headline: Half-point December hike odds jump to 11% after hot CPI
breaking.fact: Prediction-market odds of a 50bp December hike jumped to 11% from under 1% a day earlier after October CPI ran hot (+0.4% headline, +0.3% core); a quarter-point hike is still the favorite at 85%. The 2-year yield surged to 4.73% and the 10-year topped 5.00%.

breaking.headline: Texas grid crunch: 474 GW of data-center requests in queue
breaking.fact: ERCOT is weighing roughly 474 gigawatts of data-center interconnection requests as Texas tightens grid access under SB 6 and new PUCT rules. AZIO AI confirmed its Atlas One campus in Live Oak County is designed to run fully off-grid, with no pending ERCOT large-load request.

breaking.headline: AFROTECH drew 35,000 to Houston for its 10th year
breaking.fact: AfroTech Conference 2026, held Nov 2–6 in Houston, drew 35,000 attendees citywide for its 10th anniversary, focused on AI, healthcare and entrepreneurship. The conference returns to Houston Nov 1–5, 2027.

items.headline: Tankers catch fire on mines; a third blast claimed
items.body: The IRGC Navy says two tankers attempting an unauthorized southern route caught fire after hitting naval mines on Tuesday, and claims a third exploded later in the day; UKMTO also reported a tanker struck northeast of Oman's Lima. October saw 37 ships attacked in the strait — the highest monthly total since the war began, per the Washington Institute — and oil leaking from damaged tankers has reached Oman's shores.

items.headline: Saudi Bahri tankers crossing with US coordination
items.body: Saudi Arabia's main shipping firm Bahri is sending tankers through the strait in coordination with the US military — four vessels today — as the kingdom boosts Gulf loadings, with overall Middle East oil shipments now close to pre-war levels. Bahri reported a tenfold jump in Q3 net profit as tanker rates hit records, though several of its vessels were hit in security incidents.

hormuz.stats: Traffic & shares (latest verified): AIS-visible commercial traffic is running about 8% of normal — 7.0 ships a day over the past week (19 tankers) against 84.8 before the crisis. EIA puts Hormuz oil flows at 4.9M bbl/day in Q2 2026, down from 21.6M in Q4 2025; the IEA estimates ~20M bbl/day transited in 2025, about a quarter of global seaborne oil trade. China takes ~42% and India ~13% of strait crude throughput; ~90% of Iran's oil exports go to China. The EIA warns vessel-tracking data have become less reliable during the conflict.

marketsNote: Tuesday's selloff is easing into the afternoon: hot October CPI (+0.4% headline, +0.3% core) has fully priced a December Fed hike and even lifted half-point odds to 11%, while the $42B 10-year auction tailed 1bp at 5.02% on weak foreign demand. S&P ~7,517 (-0.44%), Nasdaq ~25,039 (-0.85%), Dow ~52,228 (-0.31%); VIX 19.84; 10-year 4.98%. Oil sits at two-month lows (WTI ~$86.52, Brent ~$92.12) as Trump plays down new Iran strikes. Bonds close tomorrow for Veterans Day while stocks trade.

space.headline: Starship Flight 15 set for Friday; first dual catch attempt
space.body: SpaceX rolled Super Heavy Booster 22 to Pad 2 at Starbase ahead of Flight 15, targeted for Friday, Nov 13, in a window opening at 4:45 PM CT, pending FAA approval. It would be the first flight aiming to catch both the Super Heavy booster and the Starship upper stage back at the launch site; Ship 42 would orbit 14 times over about 22 hours.

space.headline: NASA to test two lunar landers in Earth orbit before 2028 landing
space.body: NASA's revised Artemis plan has Orion carrying four astronauts on Artemis III in 2027 to rendezvous and dock with test versions of both SpaceX's Starship and Blue Origin's Blue Moon landers in Earth orbit, before Artemis IV aims to land astronauts on the Moon in 2028. Which lander flies the crew depends on test results.

space.headline: 1,600-year-old Nazca burial holds a baby born with one central eye
space.body: DNA from a tiny skull in a Nazca urn at Jauranga, Peru (AD 325–440) shows the infant girl had trisomy 13, or Patau syndrome, which caused cyclopia — a single central eye socket. It is the first such case ever identified in an archaeological context, published Nov 9 in PNAS.

weekInBrief.headline: CERN finds first evidence of a one-in-10-billion particle decay
weekInBrief.body: CERN's LHCb experiment reports evidence that the Bd meson can decay into two muons — a process predicted about once in 10 billion beauty-particle decays. Data from 2024–25 reach 3.0 sigma, 3.2 combined with older data: evidence, not yet a 5-sigma discovery. The rate agrees with the Standard Model so far, tightening constraints on new physics.

weekInBrief.headline: Webb's 'little red dots' may be the first black holes' birthplaces
weekInBrief.body: Simulations published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters suggest the James Webb telescope's enigmatic 'little red dots' are primeval galaxies hosting massive black holes formed by the collapse of supermassive primordial stars — a possible answer to how the universe's largest black holes formed less than a billion years after the Big Bang.

weekInBrief.headline: Blood test flags ovarian cancer at its earliest precancerous stage
weekInBrief.body: Hoag researchers report a first-in-the-world blood signal — elevated levels of an RNA molecule called Tu-Stroma — that identifies STIC, the precancerous stage of high-grade serous ovarian cancer. The eight-year international study, published today in Nature Medicine, could open the way to detecting the disease at its earliest biological stages.

weekInBrief.headline: Inflation is spreading: core services, food and goods all jumped
weekInBrief.body: October CPI's details were uglier than the headline: non-housing services inflation, food and core goods all rose, pushing the 10-year yield to 5.0%. The BLS index hit 337.51, implying about 4.0% year over year — though the bureau published no official year-over-year figure after last year's shutdown left October 2025 data uncollected.
